record.paper_title: Neutrino-nucleus interactions: open questions and future projects
record.context_brief: Oxygen cross sections for Megaton detectors
record.original_question: What are the precise neutrino-oxygen reaction cross sections in the several-hundred-MeV energy range needed for next-generation Megaton neutrino detectors such as Hyper-K or UNO, particularly when those detectors are used to study CP violation in the lepton sector?

evidence.quote: A precise measurement of the reactions on oxygen is of great interest also in view of the next-generation experiments involving Megaton detectors like Hyper-K or UNO [19]. In particular, their use with the aim of studying CP violation in the lepton sector would need a very precise determination of the reaction cross sections in the range of several hundred MeV.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the charged-current and neutral-current scattering of neutrinos and antineutrinos off an oxygen-16 nucleus, ν_ℓ + ^{16}O → ℓ^- + X (and the corresponding antineutrino and neutral-current channels), for incident neutrino energies in the several-hundred-MeV range (roughly 100 MeV to 1 GeV), which is the relevant kinematic regime for next-generation Megaton-scale water Cherenkov detectors used to probe leptonic CP violation through long-baseline oscillation measurements.

Determine, with quantified theoretical uncertainties, the inclusive and exclusive differential cross sections dσ/dE_ℓ dΩ_ℓ for these reactions, including the contributions of:
(i) quasielastic scattering on bound nucleons,
(ii) excitation of nuclear resonances (notably the Δ(1232)),
(iii) single-pion production and other inelastic channels,
(iv) two-body meson-exchange (2p-2h) currents, and
(v) final-state interactions of the outgoing hadrons inside the ^{16}O nucleus.

The goal is to provide a nuclear-model calculation of these cross sections precise enough (typically at the few-percent level) to support unbiased extraction of the CP-violating phase δ_CP from event rates in Megaton-scale detectors, and to identify and quantify all dominant sources of nuclear-model uncertainty (spectral function, axial form factor, RPA correlations, 2p-2h strength, pion-production model, FSI) entering the prediction.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the question was posed: dedicated measurements of neutrino-oxygen neutral-current quasielastic cross sections have been performed at Super-Kamiokande and SK-Gd using atmospheric neutrinos, and T2K/Hyper-K near-detector programs (ND280 water layers, WAGASCI, IWCD, NINJA) are systematically reducing oxygen cross-section uncertainties. However, the few-percent precision required across the full several-hundred-MeV range for unbiased CP-violation extraction has not yet been achieved; nuclear-model uncertainties (2p-2h, FSI, pion production) remain a leading systematic for Hyper-K. The problem is therefore partially solved and actively pursued.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of the neutrino-oxygen neutral-current quasielastic cross section using atmospheric neutrinos in the SK-Gd experiment
status_evidence.snippet: NCQE cross section on oxygen measured to be 0.74 ± 0.22(stat.) (+0.85/-0.15)(syst.) × 10^-38 cm^2/oxygen for 160 MeV–10 GeV.
status_evidence.claim: Recent measurements have constrained the NC quasielastic ν-^{16}O cross section but with sizeable systematic uncertainties.

status_evidence.title: A New Generation of Neutrino Cross Section Experiments: Challenges and Opportunities
status_evidence.snippet: Review of ongoing efforts to reduce neutrino-nucleus cross-section uncertainties for next-generation oscillation experiments.
status_evidence.claim: Precision oxygen cross sections at the level needed for CP-violation measurements remain an active research frontier.

status_evidence.title: Hyper-Kamiokande
status_evidence.snippet: HK combines data on carbon and oxygen (ND280, WAGASCI, IWCD, NINJA, ND280-FGD2 water layers) to enable precision cross-section studies.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple Hyper-K near detectors are being deployed specifically to pin down oxygen cross sections for CP-violation analyses.
